name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A motor vehicle designed primarily for off-highway and all-terrain use, all-terrain motorcycles included: the category an off-road e-moto falls into unless it's registered for the road.

restrictions.rule: Includes all-terrain motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles, dune buggies and any motor vehicle used on public lands for recreation; no limit on motor power or speed (Nevada Revised Statutes §490.060)
Titled and registered with the DMV within 30 days of acquiring it, for one or three years
May be ridden on any public land, trail, way or unpaved county road unless the agency over it prohibits it
Kept off paved highways except to cross one, to load or unload, in an emergency, on a trail connector of up to 2 miles, or on a highway a city or county designates for off-highway vehicles
On a highway where allowed, the rider needs a driver's license and a helmet, and it needs a headlamp, tail lamp, stop lamp and rear reflector
A city or county that designates a highway for it may require riders under 16 to be under the direct visual supervision of someone 18 or older
